If and When to Talk About Real Life Situations
You use the Present Real Conditional to talk about things you normally do in real-life situations.
You use both if and when in the Present Real Conditional.
If suggests that something happens less frequently.
If I go to a friend's house for dinner, I usually take a host gift.
When suggests that something happens regularly.
When I have a day off from work, I like to go to the mall.
Notice the structure of this type of conditional:
If / When ... Simple Present ..., ... Simple Present ...
Look at the examples from the text:
When I come downtown I take the number 30 bus.
If I am late to meet someone, I send them a text.
If I am waiting to meet someone, I keep my ringer on.
When my phone is doing many things concurrently, it malfunctions.
When I send a text, I focus on that.

Vanessa: Peter! You're 30 minutes late! What's going on? I'm really upset that you made me wait here all this time.
Peter: Sorry! When I come downtown I take the number 30 bus. Today there was an accident so the bus had to divert. It took forever to get here in the traffic. That's why I'm late.
Vanessa: Okay, well, why didn't you let me know? If I am late to meet someone, I send them a text. It's just the courteous thing to do. The reason that you're late is understandable but you need to communicate.

Peter: But I did send you a text. I sent a text when I realized that the bus was diverting. I sent it about 45 minutes ago.
Vanessa: I didn't get a text from you.
Peter: Are you sure? Do you have notifications on? Maybe you got it and you just don't realize that you did.
Vanessa: Yes, I have notifications on and my phone isn't silenced. If I am waiting to meet someone, I keep my ringer on. I would have heard if I had gotten a text. Maybe you sent it to another Vanessa.

Peter: Very funny. You're my only Vanessa. Let me check my sent messages. Look. The text, that I sent at 10:45, is right here. It's really strange that you didn't get it.
Vanessa: That is strange. Look. I got two other texts at the exact time that you sent your text. It's like it's lost in space somewhere. Were you doing anything else on your mobile at the same time? Like downloading an app or watching a video? When my phone is doing many things concurrently, it malfunctions.
Peter: No. When I send a text, I focus on that.
Vanessa: Well, you're here now. Let's get a coffee.
